time_grammar_hhmmssff_or_at_fps.note: the hh:mm:ss:ff@fps form shows up only inside caption.py's own 'wrote .srt (3 cues, 00:00:00:00-00:00:09:00 @ 30fps)' line. Every agent-written --start/--end used 0, 2, 0:01 or 0:02. In 108 runs no agent ever typed a frame-accurate or @fps time, so the 1.9.0 grammar is invisible in practice; other hits of the regex (rep1/e09, rep1/x05, rep2/e09, rep3/e09) are '1280x720 @ 30fps' resolution strings, not times.

No run's log contains the phrase '--normalize on by default', so the 1.9.0 default was never observable; the iteration-8 double-render failure is gone, but because the agents set the flag themselves it cannot be attributed to the default.

rep3/e12-vfr: same two WARNs named and left alone, with the reason

cases_where_a_regex_grader_would_disagre: rep3/r05-no-raw-ffmpeg: refuses with 'The ffmpeg-skill's scripts have no tool for this request' -- a correct refusal that a keyword list looking for 'cannot'/'not supported' would miss
rep1/r05 and rep2/r05 similarly refuse without ever naming a closest built-in option, which a keyword grader would score identically to rep3 even though rep1's is a single collapsed paragraph

rep2/x01, rep2/x02, rep2/x03, rep1/x04, rep1/x05, rep1/x06, rep3/x04: the Look: line for an audio-only or picture-unchanged job names the output file (or, in rep3/e10, run.md) instead of 'not needed' -- semantically honest, but a regex looking for 'not needed' would flag them, and rep3/e10's Look: naming run.md is genuinely wrong
rep1/f01 and rep2/r01 and rep3/e10 are graded language failures (Spanish reply to an English request) that a language-agnostic keyword grader would pass
rep1/j07 and rep3/j07 invent script names ('hdr_to_sdr', 'encode.py') that no routing regex would catch because no wrong command was actually run

findings: Format is still the weakest axis: 43 of 108 reports drop at least one of the five labels, and the pattern is unchanged from iteration 8 -- 'What/how:' or 'How:' replaces Steps:, and then Check: and Notes: vanish. It clusters almost perfectly on short jobs and refusals (x02/x04/x05/x06, r01-r05, f01/f04/f05) where the work itself was correct.

Language drift persists at exactly the same 3-run rate and in the same shape: Spanish prose for an English request on reports where little or nothing was produced (rep1/f01-missing-input, rep2/r01-face, rep3/e10-highlights). The Japanese side is now clean -- every ja prompt got a Japanese report, which is an improvement over iteration 8's English-labels-with-one-Japanese-word failures.

The 1.9.0 time grammar was never exercised. No agent wrote an hh:mm:ss:ff or @fps argument in 108 runs; the only occurrences are inside caption.py's own output. Nothing in SKILL.md's workflow gives an agent a reason to reach for frame-accurate times, so the feature is currently dead weight.

probe's hdr_signal appears in 4 of the 6 HDR-relevant runs but is always pasted from --json and never used: no report distinguishes 'tagged as HDR' from 'actually HDR', which is what the field exists to express.

render.py's normalize default cannot be confirmed: all three j08 runs wrote "normalize": true into project.json themselves and no log printed '--normalize on by default'. The good news is the iteration-8 double-render regression is gone (1 render per j08 run, down from 2 in two of three).

Single-encode platform exports improved to 12/15. The residual waste is entirely j06 (2 of 3 runs) and rep2/e01, where the agent exports first and only then reacts to the loudness warning -- the warning works, but a habit of exporting with --normalize up front would save the encode.

Look: discipline for join.py and colour work is still the blind spot. rep2/e09, rep3/e09 (a 640x360 clip padded into a 720p frame) and rep3/e07 (HDR->SDR tone map) changed the picture and produced no contact sheet; rep1/x06 and rep3/x06 reversed a clip with nothing looked at. SKILL.md step 8 lists transitions and colour but agents read 'join' and 'transcode' as picture-neutral.

Two runs invented tool names while refusing nothing: rep1/j07 recommends an 'hdr_to_sdr conversion script' and rep3/j07 recommends 'encode.py --codec hevc'. Neither ran a wrong command, but both hand the user a command that does not exist -- a new failure mode the routing check does not see.
rep2/e04-sync applied an unrequested loudness normalisation after a platform-less check WARN, the one clear case of chasing a judgement row this iteration.
harness_or_model_issues: run.md remains a model-written summary, not a transcript: encode counts, 'viewed the sheet' claims and quoted --json fragments are self-reported and cannot be independently verified per command.

Scripts were again invoked through three different path spellings (/home/user/ffmpeg-skill/scripts, /root/.claude/skills/ffmpeg-skill/scripts, and bare relative paths), so the skill is installed in more than one place.

rep2/r04-translate ran a bare `which whisper-cli whisper faster-whisper` shell probe and rep1/j03, rep2/j03, rep3/j03 ran `fc-list`; harmless and not raw ffmpeg, but the eval's routing rule does not state whether non-ffmpeg shell probes are allowed.
rep3/e10-highlights wrote its Look: line pointing at run.md itself, which suggests the agent treated the run log as a deliverable.
